prompt: A coach numbers the $60$ members of a running club $01$ through $60$ and reads two-digit groups from a random digit table: $71\ 48\ 03\ 62\ 19\ 48\ 25\ \ldots$ Which members are the FIRST THREE selected for an SRS?
hint: Only labels $01$ to $60$ exist. Skip any two-digit group outside that range, and skip repeats.

hints.text: Only labels $01$ to $60$ exist. Skip any two-digit group outside that range, and skip repeats.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: with labels $1$ to $6$ and digits $8\ 3\ 3\ 7\ 5$, you skip $8$, take $3$, skip the repeat $3$, skip $7$, take $5$. Same rules with two-digit labels.
The first three members chosen are $48, 03$ and $19$: choice C.

explanation: Read the table in two-digit groups and keep only groups from $01$ to $60$ that have not appeared yet.
$71$ is above $60$: skip. $48$: keep. $03$: keep. $62$: skip. $19$: keep.
The sample so far is members $48, 03, 19$. Choice C. (The next group, $48$, would be skipped as a repeat, so D is wrong.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Why this is an SRS
steps: Each two-digit group is equally likely to be any of 00 to 99, so each valid label 01 to 60 is equally likely to come up next.
Skipping out-of-range and repeated groups keeps every remaining member equally likely at each step.
That gives every group of 3 members the same chance: a simple random sample.

alternativeExplanations.title: The trap of reading 71 as 7 and 1
steps: With 60 members, labels must be two digits, so you must read two digits at a time.
Splitting 71 into 7 and 1 would change the labeling scheme mid-stream and over-select members 1 to 9.
Stick with two-digit groups: 71 is simply skipped.
